subject: Deal-linked GPU scaling playbook and renewal sizing
messages:
From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@skylinehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@skylinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Forecast: May-July GPU needs + renewal questions

Soojin —

Quick note from our infra team: demand for our model-driven triage has lifted dramatically over the last six weeks. I attached the Q1 run-rate export (CSV) but the short version: 95th-percentile sustained token throughput is up ~2.3x vs our renewal baseline and spikes are more frequent.

We have a renewal coming up July 31 and would like to explore an expansion that avoids immediate overcommit but gives us consistent headroom for peak days. Key asks:
- A suggested short-term buffer (we’re open to a phased add)
- Any contractual levers for burst handling vs committed capacity (credits, on-demand top-up pricing)
- Rough timeline for capacity delivery once agreed

Can we set up a 30-minute technical + commercial call this week? I copied procurement and legal as they’ll need SOW/redlines.

Thanks,
Elena Martin
Head of ML Ops, Skyline Health
elena.martin@skylinehealth.com
Attachment: Skyline_NTT_usage_report_Q1.csv
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:03:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forecast: May-July GPU needs + renewal questions

Elena — thanks for the data and the heads-up. High-level thoughts after a quick pass through the CSV: your steady-state looks healthy but the tail events are driving most of the cost and latency pain. I propose a three-part approach we can align on in the call:

1) Immediate safety corridor: add a modest, time-bound buffer equivalent to ~20% of current committed vGPU throughput to cover the 90–98th percentile spikes while we instrument more telemetry.
2) Phased expansion tied to utilization: ramp an additional chunk of capacity (we typically recommend 2-3 tranches) that only fully comes online when measured utilization crosses the agreed thresholds for two consecutive billing periods. This minimizes sunk commit while giving you runway.
3) Burst policy + credits: provide a burst pool for short-duration peaks that invoices separately at a pre-agreed uplift, with a small credit allowance applied to the first month of a tranche activation.

If that aligns, I’ll put together a mutually actionable plan and a draft SOW for quick review (target: SOW-draft-v2.pdf). Can you do Thursday 10am PT for a 30-min sync? I’ll have Ben on the call for pricing and Karthik for technical delivery timing.

Best,
— Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:45:10 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Forecast: May-July GPU needs + renewal questions

Soojin / Karthik — forwarding Elena’s baseline and my quick note. Internal only.

Short pricing/operational play I recommend:
- Immediate: provision an interim 24 A100-equivalent slots in a shared buffer pool (region us-west) for 60 days. This buys breathing room for telemetry and A/Bing scheduling policies.
- Medium: convert 60% of that buffer to reserved capacity across two 30-day tranches if Skyline’s utilization stays >75% across the tranche window.
- Safety corridor: keep a 15–20% headroom buffer in the dedicated pool for hot re-routing of latency-sensitive calls; add routing policy so noncritical batch jobs gracefully fall back to queued execution.

Notes for Karthik: can you confirm procurement lead time for an add of 24 A100 equiv (we’ll need kernel tuning and image pre-warm scripts)? If we can hit a 10–14 day lead time from approval we can align tranche-1 for early July.

I’ve attached a quick topology sketch (gpu-topology-proposal.png) and will mark up pricing ranges after Karthik confirms engineering ETA.

— Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts
Attachment: gpu-topology-proposal.png
From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@skylinehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@skylinehealth.com, legal@skylinehealth.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forecast: May-July GPU needs + renewal questions

Soojin — that approach is reasonable and pragmatic. The phased model tied to measured utilization is exactly what we were hoping for. Two quick asks before the call:

1) Can you convert Ben’s sketch into a mutual action plan with explicit milestones, acceptance criteria (utilization windows), and cancellation terms? We need that for our procurement committee.
2) Legal will want a clause for an SLA credit if latency targets degrade on >3 peak days in a rolling 30-day window during tranche activation. Please have your SOW team propose language we can review.

We’re prepared to fast-track this if delivery timing and pricing align. I’ve looped in our legal and procurement points of contact so they can join the call and sign the SOW once we agree.

Thanks — scheduling looks good for Thursday 10am PT. I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda.

Elena Martin
Head of ML Ops, Skyline Health
Attachment: SOW-draft-v2.pdf
